summary: Manually creates or rebuilds primitives from existing or newly added points. It can delete input primitives while keeping points, add new points and attributes, then create points, lines, line strips, triangles, or quads by set or pattern.

key_concepts: Primitive POP can rebuild connectivity by deleting input primitives while keeping their points and attributes.
Point and attribute sequential blocks create new geometry data before primitive blocks connect points into points, lines, line strips, triangles, or quads.
Post operations decide what happens to unused points, which is important because removal changes point indices and point-attribute alignment.
common_gotchas: Use Delete Primitives and Keep Points to rebuild connectivity from an existing point cloud without losing attributes.
By Set groups points by fixed primitive size; By Pattern uses pattern matching and is better for custom line strips.
Removing unused points changes point indices, so do it only after any index-based attributes or groups are no longer needed.
